Modified read incorporating the Beige Book

- Headline policy tone: Moderately hawkish. The Committee raised the target range to 4.50–4.75%, signaled “ongoing increases,” and continued QT; administered rates (IORB, ON RRP) were lifted accordingly, reinforcing tighter financial conditions.
- Beige Book cross-check (Jan 2023 edition): Overall activity across Districts was flat to slightly down; housing and real estate softened; wage pressures remained elevated but showed further easing; price increases moderated in more categories; labor markets were still tight but with signs of loosening; several Districts reported weaker loan demand and tighter credit availability.
- SLOOS alignment: Banks tightened C&I and CRE standards and reported weaker demand, adding de facto restraint via the bank channel.
- Policy implication: The Beige Book’s softer activity, easing wage/price pressures, and tighter credit conditions temper the hawkish “ongoing increases” guidance by underscoring cumulative tightening and lags already biting. Net tone remains slightly negative (restrictive bias) but less so than a rate/QT-only read.
